fluff.overview: The Peacemaker is a 35-ton PoliceMech produced by Irian Technologies that is a revolutionary evolution of the SecurityMech concept. Introduced in 3067, the design traces its lineage to the Star League era Peacekeeper SecurityMech, whose blueprints IrTech licensed from Coventry Metal Works. Rather than simply reproducing the aging Peacekeeper, IrTech reworked the fusion-powered design for modern urban law enforcement, most especially incorporating the experimental BattleMech Taser, a weapon ratified under the 3067 addendum to the SecurityMech Treaty, partly through IrTech's own lobbying efforts. The Peacemaker was developed as a for-sale companion to IrTech's exclusive Inquisitor SecurityMech, leveraging the Peacekeeper's established market recognition to ease customer acceptance of the new and controversial taser technology.
fluff.capabilities:
The Peacemaker is built on an IndustrialMech chassis powered by a 140-rated fusion engine, providing a top speed of approximately 65 kph. Unlike the fuel cell-powered Copper, the fusion plant allows the Peacemaker to mount energy weapons and provides indefinite operational endurance without refueling. Full environmental sealing protects the pilot from tear gas, chemical agents, and hazardous atmospheres, making the design effective in contaminated urban environments where unsealed SecurityMechs would be compromised. A searchlight in the left torso supports nighttime search and rescue operations.

The Peacemaker's conventional armament (a machine gun and SRM-2 typically loaded with rubber bullets and tear gas) is standard fare for a SecurityMech, but the design's defining feature is the BattleMech Taser mounted in the right arm. This weapon can force even the largest assault 'Mech to shut down completely, rendering the target helpless for SWAT teams or anti-'Mech infantry to neutralize. The taser fundamentally changes the Peacemaker's tactical calculus, transforming what would otherwise be a lightly armed IndustrialMech into a genuine threat to military-grade opponents. This capability has driven manufacturers across the Inner Sphere to take renewed interest in the BattleMech Taser for their own SecurityMech designs, marking the Peacemaker as a watershed in SecurityMech philosophy.
fluff.history:
The Peacemaker's development began when Irian Technologies negotiated a license for the original Peacekeeper SecurityMech from Coventry Metal Works. IrTech calculated that basing their new PoliceMech on the recognizable Peacekeeper platform would ensure market acceptance, offsetting any concerns about the untested BattleMech Taser that was central to the design. This proved to be a calculated risk, as the taser's ratification under the 3067 addendum to the SecurityMech Treaty was partly the result of IrTech's own lobbying, the company had a significant commercial interest in seeing the weapon approved for SecurityMech use.

Production began in late 3067 at IrTech's facilities on Irian, and the largest initial concentration of Peacemakers quickly appeared in the Atreus police force. The design saw its most notable early action during the Jihad, when the Atreus City Police Department's Mounted Response Unit deployed Peacemakers to maintain a quarantine cordon during the Word of Blake's chemical attack on Atreus, holding the line against the First Knights of the Inner Sphere. The Irian facilities suffered devastation during the Jihad, but the Peacemaker's production lines survived the conflict and continued operations under Republic of the Sphere oversight.

The Peacemaker's success marked a turning point in SecurityMech design philosophy. The ability to neutralize a BattleMech through a simple shutdown (without the firepower traditionally needed to defeat one in combat) opened entirely new tactical possibilities for law enforcement and security forces. Numerous manufacturers across the Inner Sphere began exploring BattleMech Taser integration for their own SecurityMech platforms, and the weapon was expected to achieve full production status in short order. The Peacemaker continues to serve police and security forces, particularly throughout the former Free Worlds League, and its influence on SecurityMech doctrine endures well beyond its own production numbers.
fluff.deployment: The sole production model of the Peacemaker, the PM-6 combines conventional SecurityMech armament (a machine gun, SRM-2, and searchlight) with the revolutionary BattleMech Taser that defines the design. Environmental sealing and a fusion engine give it operational flexibility that fuel cell-powered SecurityMechs lack, while the taser provides a credible deterrent against even heavy military 'Mechs. First produced in late 3067, the PM-6 saw its most significant early deployment with the Atreus police during the Jihad and has since spread to various law enforcement and security organizations across the Inner Sphere, as well as finding use among insurgent and criminal groups who value its asymmetric capabilities.
